newsitem.title: USA: Citicorp chairman gets smaller bonus.
newsitem.headline: Citicorp chairman gets smaller bonus.

text.p: Citicorp chairman John Reed collected a $2 million bonus in 1996, smaller than the $3 million bonus awarded in each of the two prior years, according to the proxy statement for the company's annual meeting.
A spokesman said the bonus was reduced because 1997 was merely a "good" year while the two years prior were extraordinary.

In its report on compensation, the personnel committee of the board of directors noted that Reed's salary was increased to $1.5 million annualized in March 1996 after being unchanged since March 1994.
In January, Reed was awarded 10-year options for 182,000 Citicorp shares at a cost to him of $110.50 a share.
Reed also received $88,000 in cash compensation in 1996 in connection with a savings incentive plan.
Although Reed received a smaller bonus the report listed him as owner of 1,021,624 shares. Based on Wednesday's share price, his stake is worth about $122 million.
Reed exercised options to acquire 679,000 shares in 1996 with $40.1 million in "value realised." The report said "value realised" is the market value of common stock acquired minus Reed's cost.
